definitions.explanation: A factual occurrence or observable event. Used in formal, academic, or technical contexts to describe something that has happened or been observed. More objective and analytical than {出来事|できごと}.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}{事象|じしょう}を{観察|かんさつ}する。
この{事象|じしょう}の{原因|げんいん}はまだ{解明|かいめい}されていない。
examples.english: The cause of this phenomenon has not yet been clarified.

examples.japanese: {複数|ふくすう}の{事象|じしょう}を{分析|ぶんせき}した{結果|けっか}、{共通|きょうつう}のパターンが{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: As a result of analyzing multiple events, a common pattern was found.

notes:
A formal, analytical word for events or phenomena. Commonly used in academic papers, scientific reports, and official investigations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{自然|しぜん}{事象|じしょう} (natural phenomenon)
・{事象|じしょう}を{分析|ぶんせき}する (analyze an event)
・{事象|じしょう}の{原因|げんいん} (cause of a phenomenon)
・{確率|かくりつ}{事象|じしょう} (probabilistic event — used in mathematics)

COMPARISON:
・{出来事|できごと}: everyday word for events or happenings
・{現象|げんしょう}: phenomenon, especially natural or scientific
・{事象|じしょう}: more formal and analytical than both; often used when examining events objectively
